commit_budget.note: Each order allows ONE code-bearing commit plus an optional documentation-only closeout. R5 used three and R6 has used three, so the budget is breached under BOTH — six code-bearing commits stand between the R5 baseline and this tip, and four of the six failed their own exact-SHA run. THE SIXTH IS THE COMMIT THIS RECORD LIVES IN, and it is counted rather than deferred: a record cannot name the SHA of the commit that contains it, so scripts/check-final-state.ts exempts HEAD from the ahead-of-evidence LIST and adds it back to the COUNT, printing a note whenever that allowance is in play. THE AGGREGATE USED TO STOP AT THREE, and that was an undercount produced by the record's own shape: code_bearing_commits is checked to be exactly r5_baseline..evidence_commit, so every commit made after the last GREEN run fell outside the counted range and was recorded nowhere. That is the same 'lists fewer commits than the history holds' defect R5 was rejected for, reproduced inside the field built to disclose it. commits_ahead_of_the_evidence_commit closes it, and the gate now checks that list against git in both directions. Each successor commit exists to close a failure rather than to add scope — that is the explanation and it is not a defence. R6 §5's verbatim text is NOT held in this repository (docs/orders/FBL-020-R6.md Part 2 marks it derived), so its budget is applied on the same terms as R5 §5 and is reported, not construed.
